risk.title: Earth entry at 11.48 km/s
risk.unit: peak g, shallowest non-skip-out pass (lift up)
risk.note: Shallowest corridor edge -4.25 deg: 0.8 g, ~71 W/cm^2 (first pass skips to a bound orbit; re-entry not modelled). Single-pass descent needs -7.75 deg: 15 g, ~228 W/cm^2 with constant lift-up (no bank-angle guidance modelled; real vehicles modulate lift). Limit 12.5 km/s (ESTIMATE). Fastest Earth entries flown: Stardust 12.9 km/s; Apollo ~11.0 km/s. Starship vehicle model as for aerocapture.
risk.source: Sutton & Graves 1971; NASA Stardust/Apollo entry data

pareto.note: Expected (mean) one-way crew dose, sheltered 20 g/cm^2 during SPEs; delta-v from LEO incl. capture. Direct points are a 1/3 subsample of the porkchop grid within +3 km/s of its minimum.

sources.ascent: 4.15 km/s surface->100 km LMO: Mars Sample Return MAV requirements, NTRS 20130013542; 4.2 km/s incl. 20% gravity loss: Palaszewski 2021, NTRS 20210026187 Table 3; 4.1 km/s commonly cited (Wikipedia delta-v budget)
sources.landing: Terminal propulsive descent after aero entry: 0.674 km/s (from elliptic orbit) to 0.813 km/s (from 500 km LMO, incl. deorbit), Palaszewski 2021 NTRS 20210026187 Tables 3-4 (60 t lander, beta ~750 kg/m^2). Starship value is an ESTIMATE in this range.
sources.surface_dose: MSL/RAD Gale crater, 0.64 +/- 0.12 mSv/day dose equivalent (Hassler et al. 2014, Science 343:1244797), measured Aug 2012-Jun 2013 near solar max; solar-cycle variation of the surface rate is NOT modelled (Guo et al. 2015 show ~+-25%)
sources.regolith: Geant4 Mars subsurface effective dose 121 / 67.6 / 35.0 mSv/yr at 0 / 0.5 / 1.0 m (Nucl. Sci. Tech. 2022, doi:10.1007/s41365-022-00987-2)
sources.isru: Electrical energy per kg LCH4/LO2 incl. water-from-regolith and liquefaction. Kleinhenz & Paz 2017 (AIAA 2017-0423, NTRS 20170001421): 29.7 t in 480 d at 52 kW = 20.2 kWh/kg all-electric, 35 kW with heat recuperation = 13.6 kWh/kg (central). NASA kiloton-ISRU study 2023 (NTRS 20230017069): ~230 kW for 300 t in 20 months = 11.2 kWh/kg (paper quotes ~11.5 MWh/t). 17 kWh/kg 2011 Sabatier prototype figure cited for SpaceX (Wikipedia 'SpaceX Mars transportation infrastructure'). Musk IAC 2017 implies 45 GWh / 6600 t = 6.8 kWh/kg (no breakdown; outside range).
sources.plant: Plant hardware mass per kg/day of propellant: Kleinhenz 2017 1.7 t for 61.9 kg/d -> 27.5; kiloton study 3x5.4 t pallets for ~493 kg/d -> 33 (liquefaction pallets excluded). Linear scaling to SpaceX-scale (~2-3 t/day) is an EXTRAPOLATION.
sources.power: Nuclear: Kilopower 10 kWe = 1545 kg (NTRS 20150000526 Table 4); 40 kWe FSP ~7 t (NTRS 20160014032). Solar: NASA Mars surface power white paper (2025, iparch07) 11.2-22.5 t vs 40 kWe fission-equivalent -> 280-563 kg/kWe, includes storage for night; global dust storms (tau up to 10.8) can cut output >90% for weeks - not covered by this sizing.
